subject: FintechCo - Multi-region performance follow-up & next steps

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Mike Rodriguez <mike.rodriguez@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — Multi-region inference use case

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Key goals we heard: (1) sub-150ms p95 inference in US regions for customer-facing flows, (2) sub-200ms p95 in EU for EU customers, (3) strict data residency for EU-labeled data, and (4) predictable cost per 1k tokens for routing decisions.
- Risk areas: certificate/contract language on residency, egress controls for EU test traffic, and model compatibility for their reranking workflow.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We run a 3-region performance run (us-east1, us-west2, eu-west1) using the sample prompts you provided. Redwood will provide an isolated test endpoint for the runs and a short test plan PDF attached.
2) We’ll include a hyperscaler baseline (AWS SageMaker endpoint + Azure OpenAI where applicable) so FintechCo has apples-to-apples latency and cost numbers.
3) Marissa/Sean from our team will own the test execution and results summary; we’ll share dashboards and a short recording of the runs.

Could you confirm: (a) a 2-hour window next week (preferably Wed 7/14 09:00-11:00 PT), (b) that your infra team can allow test IPs to reach your staging VPC (we’ll share IPs), and (c) whether the sample prompts contain any real PII that we should mask?

Attaching: fintechco-multi-region-test-plan.pdf, sample_prompts.json

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0126

Thanks Jordan — draft test matrix below. Attaching a short run script and the expected dashboard layout.

Test matrix (draft):
- Regions: us-east1 (N. Virginia), us-west2 (Oregon), eu-west1 (Ireland)
- Models/variants: rwd-4-8k (quantized), rwd-4-8k (fp16), aws-sage-3-large (baseline), azure-openai-gpt-like (baseline)
- Payload sizes: 128 tokens / 512 tokens / 1024 tokens
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32 concurrent requests
- Metrics captured: p50/p95 latency, failure rate, tokens/sec, egress bytes, cost-per-1k-tokens (estimated)
- Data residency handling: tag EU-labeled payloads and route to eu-west1 only; capture logs to customer-owned S3 in EU when requested (note: requires signed agreement)

Ownership: Marissa will run the Redwood endpoint tests and collect traces; Sean will run the hyperscaler baselines and produce cost comparators. We’ll produce a single slide deck and a shared Drive dashboard within 48 hours of the run.

Sean — I called out the egress/customer-owned S3 flow; we need a short blurb on how we estimate egress and any KMS considerations.

—Marissa

Attachment stubs: run_script.sh (text/x-sh), dashboard-layout.png (image/png)

Quick notes from the infra baseline perspective: 
- For the hyperscaler runs I’ll spin up SageMaker endpoints in the same regions and use equivalent instance types (p4d- or g5-equivalent) to match our throughput targets.
- Cost-per-1k calculation: include instance hourly + per-request overhead + egress estimates. I’ll add a conservative network egress line item for EU->US where applicable.
- KMS: for customer-owned buckets we’ll note that separate KMS keys and regional key policies are required; that will add a small ops overhead but keeps us compliant.

Jordan — test IPs for the Redwood test endpoint: 34.201.45.210, 34.201.45.211. Alyssa/Chris — please whitelist for Wed 09:00 PT.
